statement: Whenever min_meeting_rooms returns a result r, r is the minimum number of conference rooms required for the meetings in intervals. Equivalently, for every real number t define C(t) to be the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(intervals) and s_i <= t < e_i; then r is the maximum value of C(t) over all real t. Intervals are half-open, so an interval ending at t and an interval starting at t do not overlap.
preconditions: intervals is a slice of vectors such that 1 <= len(intervals) <= 10000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(intervals), len(intervals[i]) = 2; writing s_i = intervals[i][0] and e_i = intervals[i][1], we have 0 <= s_i < e_i <= 1000000 for every i.

statement: For every intervals satisfying the preconditions, min_meeting_rooms returns a result r; it does not panic, access out of bounds, or overflow.

statement: Whenever min_meeting_rooms returns a result r, for each i let A_i be the number of indices j with 0 <= j < len(intervals) and s_j <= s_i < e_j. Then r = max over 0 <= i < len(intervals) of A_i.

statement: Whenever min_meeting_rooms returns a result r, r is the least integer R >= 0 for which there exists a function room from the index set {i | 0 <= i < len(intervals)} to {0, 1, ..., R-1} such that for all indices i and j with room(i) = room(j), either i = j or e_i <= s_j or e_j <= s_i. Equivalently, r is the minimum number of pairwise non-overlapping groups into which the intervals can be partitioned, where empty groups are allowed.

statement: Whenever min_meeting_rooms intervals returns r and min_meeting_rooms intervals2 returns r2, r = r2.
preconditions: intervals and intervals2 are slices of vectors each satisfying 1 <= len <= 10000, each inner vector has length 2, and for every index the endpoints satisfy 0 <= start < end <= 1000000. Write s_i, e_i for intervals and s2_i, e2_i for intervals2. There exists a bijection pi from {0, ..., len(intervals)-1} to {0, ..., len(intervals2)-1} such that for every i, s2_i = s_{pi(i)} and e2_i = e_{pi(i)}.
